contentText: Syllabus (GS3):  Insurance - principles, LIC/GIC, life & general insurance, PMJAY, crop insurance, IRDAI, FDI. 1. Meaning & Principles Insurance  = legal contract against death/damage;  indemnification  = compensating the loss. Channels household savings into investment. Uberrima fides:  utmost good faith (hide nothing, e.g. HIV+ status). Indemnity:  only real loss compensated, not imaginary. Subrogation:  insurer can recover from the negligent third party after paying the insured. Causa Proxima:  loss must be directly linked (a fan can't insure an actor). Insurable interest:  insured must actually suffer if the risk occurs. Mitigation:  insured must take reasonable steps to minimise the loss. 2. History & Nationalization 1818 (European cos, racist higher premium) -> 1870 Bombay Mutual (1st Swadeshi) -> 1912 Life Insurance Companies Act -> 1938 Insurance Act (tough regulation). Year Event 1956 LIC Act took over ~245 private life insurers 1972 GIC Act took over ~107 private general insurers (4 subsidiaries) 1993 Malhotra Committee -> allowed private insurers & FDI 2025 IRDAI set up Dinesh Khara Committee to reform Insurance Act 1938 3. Life Insurance Q - Life insurance types (money returned at maturity / at death)? Type Returns Whole-life / Endowment Savings returned with interest at maturity AND on death Term life (e.g. PM Jeevan Jyoti) Low premium; NO maturity return, only paid on death ULIP (part insurance + part mutual fund) Savings returned with profit AND on death Surrender value reform (2024):  if a whole-life/endowment policy is discontinued early, 80-85% premium is now refunded (was ~zero). LIC (1956):  statutory corporation (LIC Act 1956); regulated by LIC Act, Insurance Act 1938 & IRDAI Act 1999; disinvested via IPO (2022, Govt sold 5%). Postal Life Insurance (1884) & Rural PLI (1995):  for govt/PSU/professionals & villagers (Gram Suraksha etc.). Aam Aadmi Bima Yojana (2007):  LIC scheme for BPL workers (death Rs.30k, disability up to Rs.75k). Q - PM Jeevan Jyoti vs PM Suraksha Bima (2015)? PM Jeevan Jyoti Bima (PMJJBY) PM Suraksha Bima (PMSBY) LIFE insurance (any death -> Rs.2 lakh) General/ACCIDENT insurance (accidental death -> Rs.2 lakh; limb loss Rs.1-2 lakh) Age 18-50; premium Rs.436/yr Age 18-70; premium Rs.20/yr No maturity return (term life) Suicide/alcohol death not covered 4. General Insurance & ESIC Year Public-sector general insurer 1948 ESIC (workers' health, Labour Ministry) 1957 ECGC (export credit guarantee, Commerce Ministry) 1961 DICGC (deposit insurance) 1972 GIC + 4 subsidiaries (National, New India, United, Oriental) 2002 Agriculture Insurance Company GI Nationalisation Amendment Bill 2021:  removed the 51% Govt-shareholding floor -> enables privatization of the 5 public GI companies. Q - ESIC (Employees' State Insurance Corporation)? Applies:  non-seasonal establishments with 10+ workers; subscriber salary < Rs.21,000/month; premium = employee % + employer %; covers permanent AND casual/temporary workers (NOT seasonal-industry or unorganized-sector workers). Benefits:  medical (self+family from day 1), maternity, family pension on work-death, sickness benefit, disability payment, unemployment allowance (Atal Bimit Vyakti Kalyan Yojana). Reforms:  up to 15% of corpus in equities (2022); SPREE 2025 (one-time relief for late registration); One-IP-Two-Dispensaries. 5. Health Insurance & PMJAY SAHI:  Standalone Health Insurers (only health, e.g. Star Health, Niva Bupa). Individual vs Floater:  one person vs whole family (PMJAY is a floater). Fixed vs Indemnity:  fixed payout by illness vs up to actual cost (subject to sum insured). Cashless (empanelled hospital) vs reimbursement. Q - Ayushman Bharat / PMJAY (2018)? Two parts:  1.5 lakh Health & Wellness Centres; + PM Jan Arogya Yojana (subsumed RSBY). PMJAY cover:  FREE Rs.5 lakh/family/year for secondary & tertiary hospitalization; all pre-existing diseases from day 1; cashless & paperless. Beneficiaries:  SECC data -> ~10 cr families (~50 cr people); NO cap on family size or age. Sub-schemes:  PM-SEHAT (all J&K residents), Ayushman CAPF (paramilitary), and (2024) all senior citizens aged 70+ get Rs.5 lakh (extra top-up for poor families). Runs via:  National Health Authority (NHA, health ministry); State Health Agencies. Funding: 90:10 (special-category/hilly states), 60:40 (others & UT with legislature), 100% (UT without legislature). 6. Crop & Other General Insurance PM Fasal Bima Yojana (2016):  farmer premium 1.5% (rabi) / 2% (kharif) / 5% (commercial-horticulture); rest shared by Union & State; covers pre/during/post-harvest (cyclone, unseasonal rain). 2020: made voluntary for loanee farmers; Union share cut. Also RWBCIS (weather only). NIRVIK (2019):  ECGC covers up to 90% of a bank's loss on an exporter's default (was 60%). Motor:  Third-party insurance mandatory (Motor Vehicles Act 1988); Own Damage (theft/accident/fire); free cashless treatment to accident victims up to Rs.1.5 lakh (2024). Title Insurance:  protects buyer in land-ownership disputes (RERA requires builders to buy it). Bharat Griha Raksha:  standardized fire/peril home & MSME-factory insurance.  Parametric insurance  pays on a defined trigger (e.g. earthquake magnitude), not actual-loss assessment. Cyber insurance:  covers malware, phishing, data restoration, cyber-extortion, legal defence. Reinsurance:  insurers' own insurance (Insurance Act 1938); GIC monopoly ended 2015 (Swiss Re, Munich Re allowed). Pandemic Risk Pool proposed by IRDAI. 7. IRDAI & FDI IRDAI:  set up 1996, statutory 1999, renamed 2014; HQ Hyderabad; 1 chairman + 9 members. Licenses life/general/re-insurers; grievance via Insurance Ombudsman; appeals to SAT; member of FSDC.  D-SIIs (too big to fail):  LIC, GIC, New India Assurance. Reforms:  seniors 65+ can buy new health policies; can't reject cancer/HIV patients (2024); 30-day free-look period; premium hike for seniors capped at 10%/yr. Distribution:  Bima Sakhi (women LIC agents), Bima Vahak (village salesmen), Bima Vistaar (all-in-one policy), Bima Sugam portal (2025, one-stop, NPCI-like), NHCX (fast hospital-claim exchange, 3-hr payout). Progress:  Insurance penetration = premium/GDP (~3.7%, 2023-24; global ~7%); Insurance density = premium/population (~$95). Q - FDI limits in insurance? Entity FDI limit LIC (public sector) 20% (2022) Insurance companies (except LIC) 49% -> 74% (2021) -> 100% (2025) Insurance intermediaries (agents/brokers) 100% (2020) Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha Bill 2025:  100% FDI (premium must stay invested in India); foreign insurers must join Govt schemes; IRDAI gets SEBI-like search/seizure powers. Key Facts (Quick Revision) Fact Detail LIC / GIC LIC Act 1956 (life); GIC Act 1972 (general). PMJJBY / PMSBY Rs.436 life / Rs.20 accident; both Rs.2 lakh cover. ESIC 10+ workers, salary < Rs.21k; medical+maternity+pension. PMJAY (2018) Rs.5 lakh/family/yr; no cap on family/age; SECC beneficiaries. PMFBY (2016) Premium 1.5%/2%/5%; voluntary since 2020. IRDAI Statutory 1999; HQ Hyderabad; appeal to SAT. D-SIIs LIC, GIC, New India Assurance. FDI insurance 100% (2025); intermediaries 100% (2020); LIC 20%.
